what: A3 joint rotational stiffness, solved through the GUI rather than a script
why: 8e687f0 made the GUI able to mesh at all. This run checks that the GUI and scripts/a3_joint_stiffness.py produce the same answer on the real part, which nothing had ever verified: every other committed result came from the script.

comparison_with_script.verdict: Identical to every digit reported. Same element and node counts, so Gmsh received the same geometry with the same settings; same increments and cutbacks, so CalculiX walked the same path through it. Only wall clock differs (3934 s here against 2778 s scripted), which is the machine being busy rather than anything about the solve.

caveats: Material parameters are assumed, not calibrated. The 12 MPa modulus is a placeholder and the absolute torque is not a validated prediction.

285 cutbacks across 48 increments. Identical in both runners, so this is a property of the model rather than of either runner. A cutback count far above the increment count has previously been the only visible symptom of a badly posed boundary condition on this project; resolve it before quoting 6.103.
Mesh quality: 2079 poor elements and a maximum edge ratio of 1100, on a mesh that nonetheless converged and matched the script.

files_here.manifest.json: Written by the runner: solver, mesh and material provenance.
files_here.results.dat: CalculiX reactions per increment. The final DISTAL_ROT total force at time 1.0 is the reported moment.

files_not_here.input.inp: 5.0 MB, regenerated from the STEP and the inputs above.
files_not_here.results.frd: 7.4 MB field output; not needed for the stiffness.
files_not_here.solver.log: 2.6 MB CalculiX output; increments and cutbacks above were parsed from it with core.fea.results.parse_convergence.
